A.explanation: Protons stay at 94, neutrons are $239-94=145$, and one electron is lost to give $+e$ charge, leaving 93 electrons.

B.explanation: 95 electrons would give one extra electron and a charge of $-1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, not the positive charge of W.

C.explanation: It swaps the nucleon number 239 and proton number 94, so 238 protons is impossible for $^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$.

D.explanation: It treats 239 as the proton number, but 239 is the nucleon number and 94 is the proton number.

hints: Notice the notation $^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$: identify which number is the proton number and which is the nucleon number.
Connect the ion charge $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ to the elementary charge $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ to find how many electrons were lost or gained.
Use $\text{neutrons} = \text{nucleon number} - \text{proton number}$ for $239$ and $94$, remembering ion formation changes only electrons.
walkthrough: Read $^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$: lower number $Z=94$ is proton number, upper number $A=239$ is nucleon number.
Protons are fixed by the element, so W still has $94$ protons. Neutrons are $A-Z = 239-94 = 145$.
A neutral Pu atom has electrons equal to protons, so $94$ electrons before ionisation.
Overall charge of W is $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, which equals $+1e$ since $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
A $+1e$ ion has one more proton than electrons, so one electron was removed: $94-1 = 93$ electrons.
Thus W has 94 protons, 145 neutrons, 93 electrons. This is option A.
